Forwarding my preliminary counsel notes against Acme's redlines; these are internal only — we'll draft a clean counter to send to Acme once the team agrees on scope.

On 2027-08-01 at 09:13 AM Emma Walsh <emma.walsh@acmefin.com> wrote:
> Hi Soojin,
>
> Thanks for the quick intro last week. Attached is our standard DPA with the first-pass redlines...

My inline highlights / recommendations:
- Section on transfers (Clause 6): Accept SCCs + addendum but delete open-ended routing language. Propose language: "Transfers will be limited to processors listed in Annex X, and any transfer to a jurisdiction without an adequacy decision will rely on SCCs unless otherwise agreed."
- Subprocessor notice (Clause 7): Counter-propose 14-day prior notice for non-sensitive services and 72-hour notice for emergency security patches. Offer Acme a documented objection process (submit within 10 business days) that triggers remediation or substitute services discussion.
- Data retention (Section 5): Acme's redline requires deletion within 30 days of contract termination for all backup copies — operationally heavy. Recommend a tiered approach: "For customer PII, deletion within 30 days; for operational logs and telemetry, retention up to 180 days unless specifically requested."
- Incident notification: tighten the SLA for notifying Acme to 24 hours for confirmed data breaches affecting PII; include a high-level incident report template as an appendix.
- Evidence requests: Acme asked for encryption key custodian details and SOC 2 Type II. We can provide SOC 2 Type II report under NDA and a short summary of key management practices; avoid sharing HSM config screenshots.

Risks to flag to sales: Acme's 30-day pre-approval for subprocessors may slow autoscaling / burst capacity on Dedicated pools; quantify impact if they insist.

Next steps (internal):
- Marissa to prepare annotated counterredline with the language above.
- Neha/Soojin to confirm deal impact and whether 30-day pre-approval is a deal breaker for Acme's expected throughput.
- Once counter is agreed, we share with Acme and propose a short call between counsel to resolve transfer & subproc carveouts.

Rishi
VP, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
